answer: A name typed in a minute has no pulse of its own; it only looks alive until someone checks whether work sits behind it. After a gale of look-alike wallets arrives, each claiming the same prize, the test is whether that name is still findable once the copies have burned their cheap time. An opal in a display case proves nothing. What holds is a trail of attested work and locked stake that cannot be minted as fast as aliases, so a swarm thins itself when every extra face has to pay for hours already spent.
